newsitem.title: USA: U.S. health officials launch kids' vaccine campaign.
newsitem.headline: U.S. health officials launch kids' vaccine campaign.

text.p: U.S. health authorities launched a campaign on Monday urging parents to make sure that their children have had all the shots they need.
The campaign, which has as its theme "Even If You're Sure, Ask Again", was launched by Health and Human Services Secretary Donna Shalala and Centres for Disease Control director Dr. David Satcher.

"This public service campaign is a critical tool for reminding parents to make sure they get their baby's shots on time and reminding providers to check a child's immunisation record everytime they see them," said Satcher.

Children need a series of 12 to 16 shots against 10 childhood diseases by the time they are two years old. The diseases are polio, whooping cough, diptheria, Hib meningitis, hepatitis B, measles, mumps, chickenpox, rubella and tetanus.

Health officials said that while immunisation rates for two-year-olds were at an all-time high of 75 percent and vaccine preventable diseases were at an all time low, more than one million two-year-olds were still not adequately protected.
